texts.li: {X_nameDef}, a reader of {FACTION}, has come to the gate with a stormglass in a padded case at {X_possessive} hip: a sealed vial of clear water that clouds and feathers before the sky turns. The tower at {PLACE} reads the region's weather, {X_nameDef} says, and for {COUNT} silver the Conclave would watch the colony's sky for the season: whenever a cold snap, a heat wave or worse is on its way, a vial-runner will be at the gate with the warning before it comes. Or {X_pronoun} would read tonight's sky for the colony, for nothing.

[fields] {X_nameDef}, a reader of {FACTION}, has come to the gate with a stormglass at {X_possessive} hip. The colony sows by the weather, {X_nameDef} has heard, and the tower at {PLACE} reads the weather a long way off: for {COUNT} silver the Conclave would watch the colony's sky for the season, a vial-runner at the gate before every cold snap or heat wave, and the colony's fields would know of it from the hour the runner sets off. Or a reading of tonight's sky, freely given.

[lowtech] A reader of {FACTION} named {X_nameDef} has walked from the tower at {PLACE} with a glass vial wrapped in wool. The Conclave reads the sky, {X_nameDef} says, and for {COUNT} silver it would keep watch on the colony's for a season, a runner at the gate before every hard turn of the weather. Or a reading of tonight's sky, freely given.

[industrial|spacer] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} is at the gate with a barometer, a notebook of pressure readings and a stormglass in a padded case. The tower at {PLACE} forecasts the region's weather, {X_nameDef} says: {COUNT} silver buys the colony a season of the Conclave's watch, a runner at the gate before every cold snap, heat wave or fallout. Or a free reading of tonight's sky.

[their:grateful] The Stormglass Conclave thinks well of the colony, and {X_nameDef} has come from {PLACE} to offer its watch on the colony's sky for the season, for {COUNT} silver, a runner at the gate before every hard turn of the weather. Or tonight's reading alone, as between friends.

li.label: Buy a season's watch ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: The silver is going out to {X_nameDef}, and the Conclave will watch the colony's sky for the season. {X_nameDef} has gone out to look at the colony's fields before the road.

li.label: Tonight's reading, {A_nameDef} with {X_objective}
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} is standing at the gate with {X_nameDef}, who is holding the glass up against the clouds and saying what each feather in it means.

li.label: No, thank you
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} tucks the glass away and goes back to the road, looking up at the sky as {X_pronoun} goes.

lines.li: [watch] A runner will be at your gate before the sky turns.
[watch] The glass will see it before you feel it.
[watch,fields] Show me the fields, so the warnings mean something.
[sky] Watch the glass, not the clouds, because the clouds lie.
[sky] Every sky is written down at the tower, and yours is now.
[thanks] The sky will do what it does, watched or not.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, a storm-walker of {FACTION}, has come to the gate with a brass rod over one shoulder, as tall as {X_objective}, a sealed stormglass caged at its foot. The Conclave sets its rods on the highest roofs of the region to keep a record of the storms, {X_nameDef} says, and would set one over the colony's {TALE}. It draws the lightning that falls near it down onto itself, harmlessly, and the colony would read the weather by it as well as by a weather station.

[storm] {X_nameDef}, a storm-walker of {FACTION}, has come up the road with the storm, a brass rod over one shoulder and a stormglass caged at its foot. The Conclave keeps a record of every storm, and this one is overhead: {X_nameDef} would set the rod over the colony's {TALE} now, where it would take the lightning that falls near it, harmlessly, and read the weather as well as a weather station.

[lowtech] A storm-walker of {FACTION}, {X_nameDef}, has walked from {PLACE} with a brass rod and a caged glass vial. Lightning goes where it is called, {X_nameDef} says, and the Conclave's rods call it: set over the colony's {TALE}, this one would take the strikes that fall near it, and the glass at its foot reads the weather.

[industrial|spacer] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} is at the gate with a lightning rod of the Conclave's: brass, grounded through a coil, a stormglass sealed at its foot for the tower's record. Set over the colony's {TALE}, it takes the strikes that would fall on the open ground near it, and reads the weather as well as any station.

li.label: Let them set it over the {TALE}
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} is carrying the rod in to the {TALE}, to set it up where the roof is highest.

li.label: Set it, and have {A_nameDef} learn how it is grounded
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} is setting the rod up in the {TALE}, with {A_nameDef} beside {X_objective} learning how it is grounded.

li.label: No rods on our roofs
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} shoulders the rod again and walks on toward the next roof.

lines.li: [rod] Let it come down here, and nowhere else.
[rod] Brass to the sky, and the glass at its foot.
[rod,storm] Quickly now, it will not wait for us.
[thanks] The storms will find you all the same.

texts.li: Towards evening {X_nameDef}, a reader of {FACTION}, has come to the gate with a stormglass and a lamp. {X_pronoun} has heard that {A_nameDef} keeps the colony's eye on the weather, and the Conclave teaches anyone who will learn: an evening at the glass, the clouds read against it as the light goes, and for a season after {A_nameDef} would read the weather as a reader does.

[newreader] Towards evening {X_nameDef}, a reader of {FACTION}, has come to the gate with a stormglass and a lamp. {A_nameDef} has the best hands at the colony's fields, {X_nameDef} says, and hands that know the soil learn the sky quickly: an evening at the glass, and for a season {A_nameDef} would say what the weather will do, as a reader does.

[lowtech] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come to the gate as the light goes, a glass vial wrapped in wool under one arm. The sky is read, not guessed, {X_nameDef} says, and {X_pronoun} would teach {A_nameDef} to read it tonight, the clouds against the glass, so that for a season the colony knows its weather.
[their:grateful] The Conclave thinks well of the colony, and {X_nameDef} has walked from {PLACE} at dusk to teach {A_nameDef} the glass: an evening at it, and a season of reading the weather after.

li.label: Teach {A_nameDef} to read the glass
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} is sitting with {X_nameDef} and the glass as the light goes, learning to read the one against the other.

li.label: An hour at the gate with {X_objective}, watching the sky
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} is at the gate with {X_nameDef}, the two of them watching the sky go dark.

li.label: Not tonight
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} lifts the lamp in farewell and goes back down the road.

lines.li: [glass] Watch how it feathers when the wind turns.
[glass] The glass clouds before the sky does, always.
[glass,newreader] Your hands know the soil, so your eyes can learn the sky.
[thanks] Keep an eye on the west, at least.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, a seed-carrier of {FACTION}, has come to the gate with a sack of saplings on {X_possessive} back, their roots balled in moss. The Mossborn keep a ledger of the trees round them, {X_nameDef} says, and the colony has felled {TALE} this season: every few trees felled owe the world a seedling, and {X_pronoun} has brought {COUNT} to plant on the open ground round the colony, out of its fields and its buildings.

[cleared] {X_nameDef}, a seed-carrier of {FACTION}, has come to the gate bent under a sack of saplings. The colony has felled {TALE} trees this season, and the Mossborn's ledger has noticed, {X_nameDef} says without heat: {X_pronoun} has brought {COUNT} seedlings to set in the open ground round the colony, out of its fields and its buildings, so the ledger squares a little.

[lowtech] A seed-carrier of {FACTION} named {X_nameDef} has walked from the grove at {PLACE} with saplings in a moss-lined sack. {TALE} trees have come down round the colony this season, and the Mossborn owe the world a seedling for every few: {COUNT} of them, to plant on the open ground round the colony if it will have them.

[their:grateful] The Mossborn think well of the colony, and {X_nameDef} has come from the grove at {PLACE} with {COUNT} saplings for the {TALE} trees it felled this season, to plant round it as between friends.

li.label: Let them plant the saplings
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} is setting the saplings in the open ground round the colony, one after another, a little water on each.

li.label: Plant them together, {A_nameDef} beside {X_objective}
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} and {A_nameDef} are planting the saplings round the colony, one after another.

li.label: The land is ours to clear
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} writes something in the ledger, shoulders the sack and goes.

lines.li: [plant] One for every few that fell, and the ledger squares.
[plant] Roots down, little one, and stay.
[plant,cleared] It will take more than a sack to make that right.
[refused] The ledger keeps, and so will the saplings.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, a grove-warden of {FACTION}, has come to {DEAD}'s grave with a sapling, its roots wrapped in wet moss. The Mossborn bury their dead under young trees, {X_nameDef} says, so that the one who died becomes the grove, and {X_pronoun} would plant one beside {DEAD}'s grave, with the colony gathered there if it likes.

[lowtech] A grove-warden of {FACTION} named {X_nameDef} has walked from {PLACE} with a sapling for {DEAD}. Under every grave of theirs a tree grows, {X_nameDef} says, so the dead become the grove and the grove remembers them, and {X_pronoun} would set one beside {DEAD}'s grave.

[industrial|spacer] {X_nameDef}, a grove-warden of {FACTION}, is waiting quietly by {DEAD}'s grave with a sapling in a sack of moss. The Mossborn plant a tree for each of their dead, {X_nameDef} says, and would plant one here for {DEAD}, the colony gathered or not, as it likes.
[their:grateful] The Mossborn remember the colony kindly, and {X_nameDef} came to {DEAD}'s grave the moment the grove at {PLACE} heard, with a sapling to plant beside it as for one of their own.

li.label: Plant it, the colony gathered
li.outcome: The colony is gathering at {DEAD}'s grave, where {X_nameDef} is setting the sapling into the ground beside it.

lines.li: Grow tall over them, and keep them.
They are the grove now, and the grove is long.
A root for every year they gave us.

li.label: Let {X_nameDef} plant it, {A_nameDef} beside {X_objective}
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} is planting a sapling beside {DEAD}'s grave, with {A_nameDef} there.

li.label: Leave the grave as it is
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} lays a hand on the grave a moment, and goes.

lines.li: [grove] Grow tall over them, and keep them.
[grove] They are the grove now, and the grove is long.
[refused] The ground will hold them all the same.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, a tree-connector of {FACTION}, has come to the gate with pruning hooks and a pot of resin. The colony's Gauranlen tree is spoken of in the groves, {X_nameDef} says, and the Mossborn tend every tree that has taken a person's bond: an hour or so of pruning, and its bond with the one it knows would be the stronger. {X_pronoun} would like {A_nameDef} at {X_possessive} side while {X_pronoun} works, if the colony likes.

[lowtech] A tree-connector of {FACTION} named {X_nameDef} has walked from {PLACE} with hooks and resin for the colony's Gauranlen tree. A bonded tree is a guest of the whole grove, {X_nameDef} says, and {X_pronoun} would prune it, so its bond grows the stronger.
[their:grateful] The Mossborn think well of the colony, and {X_nameDef} has come from the grove at {PLACE} to tend its Gauranlen tree, an hour's pruning for the bond's sake.

li.label: Let them tend it, {A_nameDef} at their side
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} is pruning the Gauranlen tree with {A_nameDef} beside {X_objective}, a cut at a time, resin on each.

li.label: Let them tend it
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} is pruning the colony's Gauranlen tree, a cut at a time.

li.label: The tree is ours to keep
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} bows to the tree from the gate, and goes.

lines.li: [tend] Easy now, I only take what you would drop.
[tend] A cut here, and it will reach further for you.
[refused] Tend it kindly, then, because it remembers.

titles.li: Swords for hire at the gate

texts.li: A sergeant of {FACTION}, {X_nameDef}, has come to the gate with a squad of the company, {TALE} in all, every one of them in the Banner's ash-grey. They are between contracts, {X_nameDef} says, and would hold the colony's walls for the season: camped by the colony, they take up arms against whatever comes at it while they are here. The wage is {COUNT} silver every five days, the first paid now; left unpaid, the company walks.

[raided] {X_nameDef}, a sergeant of {FACTION}, has marched a squad of {TALE} up to the gate. The colony was hit not long ago, {X_nameDef} has heard, and walls hold better with more on them: the squad would camp by the colony for the season and fight for it while they are here, for {COUNT} silver every five days, the first now. Unpaid, they strike camp and go.

[lowtech] {X_nameDef}, a sergeant of {FACTION}, has marched a squad of {TALE} up to the gate, the Banner's ash-grey on every one. The Banner fights for whoever pays and keeps its word to them, {X_nameDef} says, and would camp by the colony for the season to hold its walls: {COUNT} silver every five days, the first now. Unpaid, they strike camp and go.

[industrial|spacer] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has brought a squad of {TALE} to the gate, arms shouldered, the ash-grey of the Banner on every one. A season's contract, {X_nameDef} says: they camp by the colony and fight for it while they are here, for {COUNT} silver every five days, the first now. The Roll keeps every contract kept, and every one broken.

[their:grateful] The Ashen Banner thinks well of the colony, and {X_nameDef} has brought a squad of {TALE} to offer it first: a season camped by the colony, fighting for it, for {COUNT} silver every five days.

li.label: Hire them for the season ({COUNT} silver every five days)
li.outcome: The first wage is going out to {X_nameDef}, and the squad is making camp by the colony for the season.

li.label: No contract, but drill {B_nameDef} for an afternoon
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} is drilling {B_nameDef} at the gate, the squad looking on.

li.label: We hold our own walls
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} salutes, turns the squad about and marches them back to the road.

lines.li: [hired] Paid on the day, and we hold on the day.
[hired] The Roll has your name now, so keep it clean.
[drill] Feet first, then the blade, always the feet.
[drill] Again, and slower, and again.
[refused] The road is long, and somebody always pays.

texts.li: As the light goes, someone is waiting at the gate who will not come closer: {X_nameDef}, who marched with {FACTION} until a few days ago. {X_pronoun} left the Banner on the road, {X_nameDef} says, and the Roll will have struck the name by now; {X_pronoun} asks shelter, a corner to sleep in tonight, or a place at the colony for good.

[theirfoe] As the light goes, {X_nameDef} is waiting at the gate, a soldier of {FACTION} until a few days ago. {X_pronoun} ran from the Banner, {X_nameDef} says, and knows the Banner is no friend of the colony's: {X_pronoun} asks shelter all the same, a corner for the night or a place for good.

[lowtech] {X_nameDef}, who carried a spear for {FACTION} until a few days ago, is at the gate with the dark coming on. {X_pronoun} left in the night, and the Roll has struck the name: a corner to sleep in tonight, {X_nameDef} asks, or a place at the colony, if it will have a soldier who ran.

li.label: Take {X_objective} in
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} is one of the colony now. Word will reach {FACTION} that the colony took in one they struck from the Roll.

li.label: A night's lodging, and on the road at first light
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} has a warm corner for the night, and will be on the road at first light.

li.label: The gate stays shut
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} nods as if expecting it, and walks off into the dark.

lines.li: [taken] I will not run from this one, I swear it.
[night] A roof tonight is more than I hoped for.
[refused] No, I would not open it either.

IncidentDef.label: the Roll read at the grave

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, a keeper of the Roll of {FACTION}, has come to {DEAD}'s grave with a long book bound in ash-grey cloth. The Roll keeps the name of everyone who fell of their wounds holding a wall, of any people, {X_nameDef} says, and {DEAD}'s belongs in it: {X_pronoun} would read it into the Roll at the grave at dusk, with the colony gathered there to hear it. Or {X_pronoun} would stand a while at the grave with one of the colony.

[lowtech] A keeper of the Roll of {FACTION} named {X_nameDef} has walked from the fort at {PLACE} with the book under one arm. {DEAD} fell holding the colony's wall, {X_nameDef} has heard, and the Roll is the Banner's honour: every name of the fallen read into it aloud, at dusk, where they lie.

[industrial|spacer] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} is waiting by {DEAD}'s grave with the Roll, a ledger of every name the Banner has carried home or buried, its own people's and strangers'. {DEAD} fell of their wounds holding a wall, {X_nameDef} says, and the Roll would have the name read into it at dusk, the colony gathered.

[their:grateful] The Ashen Banner thinks well of the colony, and {X_nameDef} has come from {PLACE} with the Roll the moment the fort heard of {DEAD}, to read the name into it at the grave as for one of their own.

li.label: Read the name into the Roll at dusk, the colony gathered
li.outcome: The colony will gather at {DEAD}'s grave at dusk, where {X_nameDef} will read the name into the Roll.

li.label: Let {X_nameDef} stand a while at the grave, {A_nameDef} beside {X_objective}
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} is standing at {DEAD}'s grave with {X_nameDef} and the Roll.

li.label: We keep our own names
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} closes the book, salutes the grave, and goes.

lines.li: [roll] Held the wall, and is written so.
[roll] Every name read, and none forgotten.
[thanks] Then I will read it on the road, quietly.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, a journeyman of {FACTION}, has come to the gate with a token of burnt clay on a cord, the guild's mark. The guildhall at {PLACE} has heard of {B_nameDef}'s work, {X_nameDef} says, and commissions a {THING} of the colony's making, made at its own bench from what is in its stores. {X_pronoun} will come back for it when it is done and pay by its quality, as the guild does: about {COUNT} silver for a good one, more for better.

[art] {X_nameDef}, a journeyman of {FACTION}, has come to the gate with the guild's clay token on a cord. The guildhall at {PLACE} wants a {THING} from {B_nameDef}'s own hands, carved at the colony's table from what is in its stores, and {X_nameDef} will come back for it and pay by how fine it is: about {COUNT} silver for a good one, more for better.

[lowtech] A journeyman of {FACTION} named {X_nameDef} has walked from the guildhall at {PLACE} with a commission for {B_nameDef}: a {THING}, made at the colony's own bench. The guild pays for the work, not the hours, {X_nameDef} says, so the better it turns out the more it fetches, about {COUNT} silver for a good one.

[their:grateful] The Kiln Guild thinks well of the colony, and {X_nameDef} has come from {PLACE} with a commission for {B_nameDef}, a {THING}, paid by its quality when {X_nameDef} comes back for it: about {COUNT} silver for a good one.

li.label: Take the commission, {B_nameDef} making it
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} will make the {THING} at the bench from the stuff set apart for it, and {X_nameDef} will come back for it with the guild's silver.

li.label: No commission, but let {B_nameDef} talk shop with {X_objective}
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} is at the gate with {X_nameDef}, the two of them going over the guild's marks and the colony's work.

li.label: We make for ourselves
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} tucks the clay token away and goes back to the road.

lines.li: [commission] Put your mark on the base when it is done, small.
[commission] The guild pays for the work, not the hours.
[refused] The guildhall's door stays open to you.

IncidentDef.label: the guild comes for the commission

texts.li: [maker] {X_nameDef}, the journeyman of {FACTION}, is back at the gate for the {THING} {A_nameDef} made for the guild. It turned out {TALE}, and the guild pays by the work: {COUNT} silver for it.

[!maker] {X_nameDef}, the journeyman of {FACTION}, is back at the gate for the {THING} made at the colony's bench for the guild. It turned out {TALE}, and the guild pays by the work: {COUNT} silver for it.

[masterwork] {X_nameDef}, the journeyman of {FACTION}, is back for the {THING} the guild commissioned. It turned out {TALE}, and {X_nameDef} turns it in the light a long while before naming the price: {COUNT} silver, as the guild pays for work like this.

li.label: Hand it over for {COUNT} silver
li.outcome: The {THING} was carried out to {X_nameDef}, who looked it over a long while and paid the {COUNT} silver.

li.label: Hand it over, and have {A_nameDef} hear what the guild sees in it
li.outcome: The {THING} is going out to {X_nameDef}, and {A_nameDef} is at the gate with {X_objective}, hearing what the guild saw in it and what it would do better.

li.label: Keep it after all
li.outcome: The colony kept the {THING}. {X_nameDef} marked it in the guild's book as a commission not kept, and went home with an empty pack.

lines.li: [bought] Good work, and the guild will say so.
[bought] Marked and paid, as the guild does.

texts.li: [maker] {X_nameDef}, master-trader of {FACTION}, has come a long way on word of a masterwork at the colony, and has been to look at it: "{TALE}", the {THING} {A_nameDef} made. The guild buys the best work of the region for its hall at {PLACE}, and bids {COUNT} silver for it, well over what any trader would give.

[!maker] {X_nameDef}, master-trader of {FACTION}, heard of the colony's "{TALE}" on the road and has been to look at it. The guild keeps the finest work of the region in its hall at {PLACE}, and bids {COUNT} silver for the {THING}, well over its worth to a trader.

[legendary] {X_nameDef}, master-trader of {FACTION}, stood a long time before "{TALE}" without a word. Work like that comes along once in a guild's lifetime, {X_nameDef} says at last, and the hall at {PLACE} would give it a place of honour: {COUNT} silver for the {THING}, far more than any trader would give.

[lowtech] A master-trader of {FACTION}, {X_nameDef}, has walked from the guildhall at {PLACE} on a rumour of the colony's "{TALE}", and found it true. {COUNT} silver for the {THING}, {X_nameDef} offers, for the guild's hall.

li.label: Sell "{TALE}" for {COUNT} silver
li.outcome: The {THING} was carried out to {X_nameDef}, who paid the {COUNT} silver there and then and packed it in straw for the road.

outcomes.li: [standing] The {THING} was taken up from where it stood and carried out to {X_nameDef}, who paid the {COUNT} silver and packed it in straw for the road.

li.label: Keep it
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} took a last long look at "{TALE}". Word of it will reach the guildhall at {PLACE}, and the colony's work will be talked of there.

li.label: Send them on
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} bows and goes, without another word about the piece.

lines.li: [view] Look at the line of that, just there.
[view] The guild has nothing finer in the hall.
[bought] The hall will be proud of this one.
[kept] Keep it well, because it deserves keeping.
[refused] The guild will ask again, some year.
